cases.title: Help question: what a red LOS light on the modem means, answered from the help articles

articles.title: What the lights on your modem mean
articles.text:
Each light on your modem tells you something about your connection.

Power is on when the modem has power. If it is off, check that the power adapter is plugged in and that the outlet works.

PON shows the connection to our network. Steady means the modem is connected. Blinking means it is still trying to connect.

LOS means loss of signal, and it is normally off. A red or blinking LOS light means no signal is reaching the modem through the fiber line.

LAN is on or blinking when a device is plugged into the modem with a cable.

WLAN is on or blinking when the modem's Wi-Fi is on.

If the LOS light is red or blinking, here is what you can do.

First, check the thin fiber cable that goes into the back of the modem. It should be firmly plugged in, and not bent, pinched or pulled tight. Do not unplug it, and never look into the end of the cable.

Next, restart the modem: turn it off, wait a few seconds, and turn it back on.

If LOS is still red or blinking once the modem has started up again, the problem may be on the line outside your home or in your area. Tell us on the hotline, and we can check your connection.

articles.title: Restarting your modem yourself
articles.text:
Restarting the modem clears many small problems, such as a slow or dropped connection.

Press the power button on the modem to turn it off, or unplug its power adapter. Wait a few seconds, then turn it back on.

Give the modem a few minutes to start up. The Power light comes on first, and the PON light turns steady once the modem is connected again.

Do not press the small reset hole with a pin. That erases your Wi-Fi name, your password and the modem's other settings.

articles.title: Moving to a new address
articles.text:
If you are moving, tell us before you move.

Our team first checks whether we have service at your new address. If we do, they arrange for a technician to move your connection there.

Keep your modem and its power adapter, and take them with you. Do not cut or unplug the fiber cable at your old home yourself.

grade.notes: Replies are English-led with po and a short 'Sandali lang po', and the goodbye matches the style. The second and third turns run a bit long: the explanation packs in extra steps, and the 'call us on the hotline' line is odd when the caller is already on the hotline. Taglish is natural but fairly light, which fits the style.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber. This is Tala, an AI assistant, and this call is recorded for quality. How can I help you po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hello po! Ah, may general question lang ako. Kanina kasi sa modem ko, nag-blink na red yung LOS light for a while. Okay na siya ngayon, pero ano ba talaga ibig sabihin nung red LOS?

transcript.text: Sandali lang po, let me check.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: A red LOS light means "loss of signal" po, so no signal was reaching your modem through the fiber line. If it shows up again, check that the thin fiber cable at the back is firmly plugged in and not bent or pinched, then restart the modem. Is it working fine now po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ah okay po, gets. Yes po, working na siya ngayon. So pag nag-red ulit, check ko lang yung fiber cable if nakasaksak nang maayos at hindi bent, tapos i-restart ko yung modem, tama po? And what if hindi pa rin nawala yung red?

transcript.text: Tama po. If the red LOS is still there after the restart, the problem may be on the line outside your home or in your area, so please call us on the hotline and we can check your connection. Is there anything else I can help you with po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ah okay po, malinaw na. Thank you po sa help, Tala! Sige po, bye na.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: You're welcome po. Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber.

cases.title: Scenario 1: Batasan Hills outage, cause and restoration time

grade.notes: Replies are short, spoken-style, and professional, with the correct 'Sorry to hear that po', a tool-call line, and a proper goodbye. Taglish stays English-led with 'po' and set phrases; 'Verified na po kayo' is slightly more Tagalog than ideal, and 'Sige po' is fine. She stays courteous and patient through the caller's confusion, and only gives the last four digits.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber. This is Tala, an AI assistant, and this call is recorded for quality. How can I help you po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hello po, magandang umaga. Wala pong internet ang bahay namin since kanina pong umaga. Gusto ko lang pong malaman kung bakit at kailan babalik.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Sorry to hear that po. May I have your Kidlat Fiber account number and the last four digits of your registered mobile number so I can verify your account?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Opo, ang account number ko po ay ******5601. Tapos yung last four digits ng mobile number ko po ay 0101.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Thank you po. Sandali lang po, let me verify your account.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Verified na po kayo, Maria. Let me check your area for outages now.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: There's an outage in your area po, caused by a fiber cable cut along Batasan Road during road works. Service is expected back around 4:15 AM today.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ah, ganun po ba. Pero po, umaga na ngayon at wala pa rin kaming internet. Sigurado po ba kayo sa 4:15 AM? Baka po 4:15 PM yung ibig ninyong sabihin?

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: The system shows 4:15 AM po, and I can't change or guess that time. It's an estimate, so if you still have no internet after that, please call us again and we'll check your connection. Would you like the outage reference po?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Ay, ganun po ba. Eh kasi po nakakalito, kasi lampas na po ng 4:15 AM ngayon. Ibig sabihin po ba, bukas ng madaling araw pa babalik? Para po alam ko kung maghahanap ako ng ibang paraan para makapagtrabaho.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Sorry po for the confusion. Let me check the outage again to see if there's an updated time.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: The system still shows the same estimate po, 4:15 AM today, and I have no newer time. I can't say it will be tomorrow, so if you need to work now, it's safer to have a backup like mobile data. Would you like me to text you the outage reference?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sige po, salamat sa pag-check. Mag-mobile data na lang muna ako. Opo, pakitext na lang po yung outage reference. Salamat po, paalam na po.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: Sige po, I'll text it to you now.

transcript.speaker: tala
transcript.text: You're welcome po. I sent the outage reference to your mobile ending in 0101. Thank you for calling Kidlat Fiber.
